questions.prompt: What is the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied called?
What happens when the market price is above the equilibrium price?

choices.text: Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, so a surplus puts downward pressure on the price
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so a shortage pushes the price even higher
The supply curve shifts to the left, so equilibrium is restored right away
The demand curve shifts to the right, so buyers purchase the leftover goods

questions.prompt: Other things being equal, both demand and supply for a good increase at the same time. What can you say for sure about the equilibrium?

choices.text: The equilibrium price rises, and quantity may go either way
The equilibrium quantity falls, and price may go either way
The equilibrium price falls, and quantity may go either way
The equilibrium quantity rises, and price may go either way

questions.prompt: The demand function is Qd = 120 − 3P and the supply function is Qs = 20 + 2P. What is the equilibrium price? (Enter a number only.)
